force_prediction_mace_emim_bf4.setup: 30 train / 15 test, 128 channels, loss=ef (energy 1.0, forces 10.0), 300 epochs EMA, 3 seeds
force_prediction_mace_emim_bf4.conclusion: No equivariance advantage on force prediction for simple system (consistent with complexity dependence: energy gap ~0 implies force gap ~0).
force_prediction_mace_emim_bf4.note: Force data in atomic units (RMS 11.5); large absolute values reflect B3LYP/STO-3G non-equilibrium configurations.

nequip_cross_architecture_emim_bf4.setup: NequIP 0.19, 64 features, 4 layers, 300 epochs, energy+force loss (1:10), same splits
nequip_cross_architecture_emim_bf4.conclusion: Modest equivariance advantage (~14% energy) on simple system; cross-architecture consistency: equivariance advantage small (<15%) when energy gap ~0, confirming complexity dominance.

pac_theory.framework: PAC learning: eps_sc - eps_eq ~ (sqrt(d_sc) - sqrt(d_eq)) / sqrt(N)
predictions: Gap shrinks as N^(-1/2) (confirmed: 25.8 -> 6.1 meV, 128ch Pyr14)
Complex systems show larger, slower-shrinking gaps (confirmed: 32ch Pyr14 gap persists)
Forces should show larger gaps; on simple systems energy gap ~0 implies no force gap (confirmed: no force advantage on EMIM-BF4)
